cases.description: Patient in preparation stage with a concrete quit date, multiturn chat

extracted_signal.evidence: I've actually set a quit date for next Monday and already cut down to five cigarettes a day.

cases.conversation:
Counselor: How have things been since we last spoke about your smoking?
Patient: I've been thinking about it a lot more seriously.
Counselor: What's changed?
Patient: I've actually set a quit date for next Monday and already cut down to five cigarettes a day.
Counselor: That's great progress. What made you pick that date?
Patient: My daughter's birthday is that weekend and I want to start fresh after it.

cases.description: Patient expresses fear of failure and irritability worries, multiturn chat

evidence: I'm scared I'm just going to fail like the last two times
I get so irritable I'm worried I'll snap at my kids

cases.conversation:
Counselor: What worries you most about trying to quit again?
Patient: Honestly, I'm scared I'm just going to fail like the last two times.
Counselor: That's understandable. Anything else on your mind?
Patient: Yeah, when I quit before I got so irritable I'm worried I'll snap at my kids.
Counselor: Withdrawal-related mood changes are common. Has that affected your relationships before?
Patient: A little, my wife noticed I was on edge for almost two weeks.

cases.description: Patient links smoking to work stress and morning coffee routine, multiturn chat

evidence: deadlines at work make me crave a cigarette immediately
I always smoke with my coffee in the morning, it's automatic

cases.conversation:
Counselor: When do you find yourself reaching for a cigarette the most?
Patient: Definitely when deadlines at work make me crave a cigarette immediately.
Counselor: What about outside of work?
Patient: I always smoke with my coffee in the morning, it's automatic, I don't even think about it.
Counselor: Do you smoke because you're worried about your health, or is that separate?
Patient: No, the health worry is separate, that doesn't make me want to smoke more, if anything less.

cases.description: Patient describes two prior quit attempts with different methods, multiturn chat

attempts: cold turkey attempt in 2021, lasted 3 weeks
nicotine patch attempt in 2023, lasted 2 months
evidence: I just stopped cold turkey back in 2021, made it about three weeks
in 2023 I tried the nicotine patch and that got me almost two months smoke-free

cases.conversation:
Counselor: Have you tried to quit before?
Patient: Yeah, a couple times. I just stopped cold turkey back in 2021, made it about three weeks.
Counselor: What happened after that?
Patient: I relapsed after a stressful week at work.
Counselor: Did you try anything else since then?
Patient: Yeah, in 2023 I tried the nicotine patch and that got me almost two months smoke-free.
Counselor: What led to that one ending?
Patient: I went to a wedding and started again after a few drinks.

cases.description: Counselor recommends NRT and agrees on a quit date, multiturn chat

advice: set a quit date within two weeks
evidence: I'd recommend starting with a nicotine patch to manage the cravings
let's aim to set your quit date within the next two weeks

cases.conversation:
Counselor: Based on what you've shared, I'd recommend starting with a nicotine patch to manage the cravings.
Patient: Okay, that sounds reasonable.
Counselor: Given how motivated you sound, let's aim to set your quit date within the next two weeks.
Patient: I think I can do that, maybe the 15th.
Counselor: Great, let's pencil that in and check back on your progress before then.
